passages.text: After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, as well as the officials of Judah and the craftsmen and metalsmiths from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon, the LORD showed me two baskets of figs placed in front of the temple of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
He took Jeconiah away from Jerusalem.
Jeconiah was the son of Jehoiakim.
Jeconiah was king of Judah.
Nebuchadnezzar also took the officials of Judah.
He took the craftsmen and metalsmiths from Jerusalem.
He brought all these people to Babylon.
After this, the LORD showed me something.
I saw two baskets of figs.
The baskets were placed in front of the temple of the LORD.
passages.original: הִרְאַנִי֮ יְהוָה֒ וְהִנֵּ֗ה שְׁנֵי֙ דּוּדָאֵ֣י תְאֵנִ֔ים מוּעָדִ֕ים לִפְנֵ֖י הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה אַחֲרֵ֣י הַגְל֣וֹת נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֡ל אֶת־ יְכָנְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־ יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָה֩ וְאֶת־ שָׂרֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֜ה וְאֶת־ הֶחָרָ֤שׁ וְאֶת־ הַמַּסְגֵּר֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיְבִאֵ֖ם בָּבֶֽל׃

passages.text: One basket had very good figs, like those that ripen early, but the other basket contained very poor figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
passages.sermon:
The LORD showed Jeremiah two baskets of figs.
One basket held very good figs.
These figs were like the early, first figs of the season.
The other basket held very bad figs.
These bad figs were so spoiled that no one could eat them.
passages.original: הַדּ֣וּד אֶחָ֗ד תְּאֵנִים֙ טֹב֣וֹת מְאֹ֔ד כִּתְאֵנֵ֖י הַבַּכֻּר֑וֹת וְהַדּ֣וּד אֶחָ֗ד תְּאֵנִים֙ רָע֣וֹת מְאֹ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ תֵֽאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹֽעַ׃ס

passages.text: “Jeremiah,” the LORD asked, “what do you see?” “Figs!” I replied. “The good figs are very good, but the bad figs are very bad, so bad they cannot be eaten.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He called me by name.
He said, "Jeremiah, what do you see?"
I answered Him.
I said, "I see figs."
Some figs are very good.
Some figs are very bad.
The good figs are very good.
The bad figs are very bad.
The bad figs are so bad that no one can eat them.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י מָֽה־ אַתָּ֤ה רֹאֶה֙ יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ וָאֹמַ֖ר תְּאֵנִ֑ים הַתְּאֵנִ֤ים הַטֹּבוֹת֙ טֹב֣וֹת מְאֹ֔ד וְהָֽרָעוֹת֙ רָע֣וֹת מְאֹ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹֽעַ׃פ

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Like these good figs, so I regard as good the exiles from Judah, whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a message.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He said, “These good figs are very good.
I see the exiles from Judah as good, just like these figs.
I sent these people away from this place.
I sent them to the land of the Chaldeans.
I did this for their good.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כַּתְּאֵנִ֥ים הַטֹּב֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה כֵּֽן־ אַכִּ֞יר אֶת־ גָּל֣וּת יְהוּדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר שִׁלַּ֜חְתִּי מִן־ הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה אֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים לְטוֹבָֽה׃

passages.text: I will keep My eyes on them for good and will return them to this land. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks about the exiles from Judah.
The LORD says, “I will watch over them for their good.
I will bring them back to this land.
I will build them up.
I will not tear them down.
I will plant them.
I will not uproot them.”
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י עֵינִ֤י עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לְטוֹבָ֔ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֖ים עַל־ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את וּבְנִיתִים֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶהֱרֹ֔ס וּנְטַעְתִּ֖ים וְלֹ֥א אֶתּֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: I will give them a heart to know Me, that I am the LORD. They will be My people, and I will be their God, for they will return to Me with all their heart.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God will give the exiles from Judah a new heart.
This new heart will help them know God.
They will understand that God is the LORD.
They will become God’s people.
God will be their God.
They will return to God with all their heart.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּי֩ לָהֶ֨ם לֵ֜ב לָדַ֣עַת אֹתִ֗י כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיוּ־ לִ֣י לְעָ֔ם וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִ֑ים כִּֽי־ יָשֻׁ֥בוּ אֵלַ֖י בְּכָל־ לִבָּֽם׃ס

passages.text: But like the bad figs, so bad they cannot be eaten,’ says the LORD, ‘so will I deal with Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem—those remaining in this land and those living in the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about Zedekiah, king of Judah.
Zedekiah is the ruler of Judah.
He has officials who serve under him.
There is a remnant of people from Jerusalem.
Some of these people remain in the land of Judah.
Some of these people live in the land of Egypt.
The LORD compares them to bad figs.
These figs are so bad that no one can eat them.
The LORD will treat Zedekiah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem like these bad figs.
The LORD will deal with them because of their great evil.
passages.original: וְכַתְּאֵנִים֙ הָֽרָע֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹ֑עַ כִּי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כֵּ֣ן אֶ֠תֵּן אֶת־ צִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֤ה וְאֶת־ שָׂרָיו֙ וְאֵ֣ת׀ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִים֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְהַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: I will make them a horror and an offense to all the kingdoms of the earth, a disgrace and an object of scorn, ridicule, and cursing wherever I have banished them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people He has banished.
God will make these people a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
God will make them an offense to every nation.
They will become a disgrace wherever they go.
People will scorn them in every place.
People will ridicule them everywhere they are sent.
People will use them as an example for cursing in all lands.
God will do this in every place where He has driven them.
passages.original: וּנְתַתִּים֙ לִזְוָעָה לְרָעָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ לְחֶרְפָּ֤ה וּלְמָשָׁל֙ לִשְׁנִינָ֣ה וְלִקְלָלָ֔ה בְּכָל־ הַמְּקֹמ֖וֹת אֲשֶֽׁר־ אַדִּיחֵ֥ם שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: And I will send against them sword and famine and plague, until they have perished from the land that I gave to them and their fathers.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke about the people of Judah.
God said He would punish them.
God said, “I will send the sword against them.
I will send famine against them.
I will send plague against them.
I will do this until they are gone from the land.
I gave this land to them and to their fathers.
They will perish from this land.”
passages.original: וְשִׁלַּ֣חְתִּי בָ֔ם אֶת־ הַחֶ֖רֶב אֶת־ הָרָעָ֣ב וְאֶת־ הַדָּ֑בֶר עַד־ תֻּמָּם֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥תִּי לָהֶ֖ם וְלַאֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃פ
